answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and place them on the bottom; shuffle the nine Conflict II and deal five on top; shuffle the three Conflict I and deal one on top. This makes a 10-card deck (1 I, 5 II, 4 III). Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking.
answers.evidence: Setup: Create the Conflict Deck.

answers.answer: Four-player human: score starts at 1; three-player: score starts at 0. Both start with two Agents on the Leader (the third/Swordmaster beside the board), three troops in their garrison (nine in supply), and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: score marker is 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents; three troops in garrison; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but after your Reveal your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take a later Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from cards revealed in the Reveal turn, not cards played on Agent turns. Clean Up moves all cards in front of you from both types of turns to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent turns are optional; after Reveal, turns are skipped; Resolve Reveal Effects and Clean Up.

answers.answer: No. Entry costs and requirements must be paid before resolving effects from the space or played card. One card sends one Agent using one chosen Agent icon; a card without Agent icons can only be revealed, not used on an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs immediately before resolving effects; choose only one Agent icon; cards without icons only on Reveal.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited this turn plus up to two of the four already in your garrison, for five total. A non-Combat destination allows no deployment. Recruited troops come from your personal supply and are placed in your garrison before deployment.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: recruit from supply to garrison; at Combat spaces deploy all recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any board space connected to one of your Spy-occupied observation posts without recalling that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to ignore another player's Agent and occupy that same space; Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy when you send an Agent to draw a card, chosen immediately after placing the Agent and before space/card effects. The same Spy cannot be used for both; separate Spies can do Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence on one placement. Gather Intelligence must be chosen at that immediate timing point.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts; FAQ & Rulings: Spies.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops = 4, one sandworm = 3, and four swords = 4. If your final unit is removed, strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict, you are not eligible to play Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; no unit means strength 0. Combat phase: players with at least one unit may play Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not prevent you acting again if another player plays; the window closes once all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison) and sandworms return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: you are not required to pass just because you passed earlier; consecutive passes close window. Combat cleanup.

answers.answer: With four players, two tied for highest each take the second reward, neither wins or takes the Conflict card; the remaining players compete for the third reward. With three players or fewer, the same tie for first gives each tied player the second reward, no one wins or takes the card, and no other rewards are given. A zero-strength player receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties; Resolve Combat: zero strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; two worms do not quadruple them. Control and battle icons cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice for 1 VP, the doubled reward permits paying the cost a second time: pay 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 spice for 2 VP.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more worms; control and battle icons excluded; optional cost may be paid a second time (3 spice for 1 VP, or 6 for 2).

answers.answer: When you win and take a Conflict card into your supply, check for a matching face-up Conflict or Objective card. Matching is mandatory: flip both face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, you may match the wild icon to any one of the three icons in your supply, flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: check upon winning; matching pair must be flipped; Endgame wild icon may match any of three.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; lose it below 2 and regain it upon returning to 2. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained if Influence later drops below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. First to 4 also takes the Alliance and its 1 VP; that VP follows the token. Merely tying the holder at 4 does not take it; an opponent must rise higher.
answers.evidence: Scoring: Faction Influence, including separate reversal rules for track bonus and Alliance VP; tying does not steal.

answers.answer: Persuasion may be spent before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool it from sources to buy one card and split one source across cards. The Row is refilled immediately, so you may buy its replacement if able. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: spend Persuasion before/between/after effects. Acquiring Cards: pool/split, replace Row, acquired card to discard.

answers.answer: At Makers, each unoccupied Maker space (Deep Desert, Hagga Basin, Imperial Basin) gains one bonus spice, accumulating between rounds; visiting gains all bonus spice there. Summoning a worm is blocked at a Conflict protected by the Shield Wall. Hooks are normally required only when the effect specifies them; Hooks are retained, not spent. A summoned worm goes directly to your Conflict quadrant and can never be placed in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers; Sandworms; Maker Hooks are not universal prerequisite and never spent; worms cannot be placed in garrison.

answers.answer: At Recall, at the end of a round, 10+ VP by any player or an empty Conflict deck triggers Endgame. Players may first play and resolve Endgame Intrigue, then compare VP. Tiebreakers are spice, Solari, water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Phase 5: Recall; Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup: shuffle 20 contracts, place two face up and the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Add four CHOAM Intrigue cards to that deck and four CHOAM Imperium cards to that deck. Shaddam is optional, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix compatibility and stay out of standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module setup changes; Components identifies the 10 contrasting-back tokens as Rise of Ix only.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it face up from the bank; if all are taken, it gives 2 Solari. Harvest is completed by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the stated total spice that turn, including other sources. Immediate completes as soon as taken. Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Taking contracts; Completing contracts.

answers.answer: No. If you take a contract for a board space after already sending your Agent there that turn, you must wait for a future turn; you must hold it when sending the Agent. Upon completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Completing contracts: already sent Agent means wait; announce, gain rewards, flip face down in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the other two eligible Objectives are dealt randomly to humans, and the First Player marker goes to the human whose Objective shows it. Order is First Player → Rival → other human; First Player alternates only between humans. The Rival takes Agent turns and never a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup; Agent turns.

answers.answer: The Rival ignores an occupied destination and reveals another Hagal card. For a two-destination card it uses only the destination matching the current condition (Guild Influence or Conflict tier); if occupied, it draws again and cannot use the other destination. It ignores ordinary space costs and effects, applying only Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, reshuffle immediately and continue.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns; ignore normal space costs/effects; reshuffle House Hagal if empty or Reshuffle appears.

answers.answer: Shuffle Objectives after removing any cards whose 1-3P or 4/6P marking does not match the player count; each player draws one at random. This applies to standard three- and four-player setup. The holder of the Objective showing the First Player marker starts. Shaddam is not used unless playing with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5.

answers.answer: Bank resources and sandworms are not limited; make a convenient substitution if the bank runs out. If your personal troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit more until troops return to it. Resource payments are not specified as going to a particular destination in the summary.
answers.evidence: Setup: bank resources are not meant to be limited; make convenient substitution. Recruiting: empty troop supply prevents recruitment until troops return.

answers.answer: Five phases: Round Start (reveal Conflict, then draw five cards); Player Turns; Combat; Makers; Recall. At Recall, if Endgame is not triggered, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Player Reference list all five phases and Recall.

answers.answer: Yes, board-space effects, Agent-box effects, and Faction Influence may be resolved in any order. No, the visit's Influence cannot meet its own entry requirement: costs and requirements must be met before resolving effects.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: effects may be carried out in any order; entry costs/requirements paid before effects.

answers.answer: No. An arrow cost and effect can be used only once per turn, except sandworm reward doubling on a Conflict reward. Effects are generally mandatory; optional “may” effects, optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon may be declined. A direct instruction to trash itself is mandatory, and Intrigue conditions/costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ & Rulings: Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If none remain in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If the placement effect specifies an Agent-icon type, the chosen post must connect to a space with that icon or the Spy cannot be placed.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: You cannot Infiltrate your own occupied board space: Infiltrate is for ignoring another player's Agent. You cannot use a Spy without playing a card for the Agent turn. You may recall two different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, but cannot use two to Gather Intelligence on the same placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts; FAQ & Rulings: Spies.

answers.answer: The controller of Arrakeen or Spice Refinery gains 1 Solari whenever any player, including the controller, visits; Imperial Basin's controller similarly gains 1 spice. Winning a Conflict titled for one of these locations puts your Control marker there, replacing the opponent's marker. When a Conflict is revealed for a location you already control, you may deploy one defensive troop from your supply.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control; Board Space Guide entries for Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, Imperial Basin.

answers.answer: In a three-player game, a tie for second gives each tied player the third reward; the Conflict winner keeps their rewards and card, with no further rewards. A tie for third in four players receives nothing. If three or more tie for first in four-player play, all tied players receive the second reward and no one wins/takes the card; no other rewards are given.
answers.evidence: Combat ties.

answers.answer: In three-player play, three different positive strengths receive first, second, and third rewards. The Rival uses normal two-/three-player reward and tie rules, so its participation does not change the standard three-player reward structure.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat; Required Rival Rules: Combat cleanup and two-/three-player reward and tie rules apply normally.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat; Endgame Intrigues at the end of the game. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, until played; after resolving, place face up in the Intrigue discard pile. If the Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discard pile to form a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards; FAQ & Rulings: Draw timing.

answers.answer: No, an ordinary discard instruction cannot discard an Intrigue unless it says so. An ordinary discard comes from your hand. Secrets gives you one Intrigue selected at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Secrets board-space entry: selected at random.

answers.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play. Ordinary trashed cards go to the box; Reserve cards return to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or directed to trash itself. The Spice Must Flow's acquired VP remains even if the card is later trashed.
answers.evidence: Trashing; FAQ & Rulings: Victory.

answers.answer: Acquire-box effects resolve once, at the moment the card is acquired. Reshuffle your discard pile into a new deck whenever you cannot draw because your deck is empty. Unused Persuasion cannot be saved and is lost after your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed during Reveal remain in play until Clean Up, unless trashed first. A Fremen Bond card may use its effect if you have one or more other Fremen cards in play; two Bond cards can activate one another regardless of play order. They cease to be in play at Clean Up.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent placed this turn; it can be used on another Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop returns to your garrison. “Retreat any number” may mean zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ & Rulings: Combat and troops.

answers.answer: An effect granting two Influence with a free choice means choose one Faction and gain both there; it cannot be split. An Alliance-icon effect requires holding that Faction's Alliance token. A minimum-Influence effect requires meeting its stated threshold with the specified Faction.
answers.evidence: Influence: free-choice two cannot be split; Alliance and minimum Influence requirements.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied, a formerly tied player takes the Alliance; if multiple were tied, the former holder chooses which one receives it. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board. The old holder loses the Alliance VP.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Alliance loss.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. One drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, when you draw five additional cards. A Plot Intrigue played earlier with a Reveal-time effect stays face up until then, is used, then discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Draw timing.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Combat and troops.

answers.answer: If VP and all four listed resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed track's 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Victory.

answers.answer: No. Fulfill all contracts held for the same space with one Agent placement; they cannot be delayed. A board-space contract is another effect of that Agent turn and resolves in any order with space and Agent-box effects, but it must have been held when the Agent was sent.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Contract completion is mandatory.

answers.answer: No. Shaddam's set-aside Sardaukar contracts do not start in his possession; Sardaukar Commander lets him choose one instead of a generally available contract when acquiring a contract. Emperor of the Known Universe applies immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent and lasts only that turn, not the round.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Shaddam.

answers.answer: Feyd's Training token starts on the leftmost track space and stays on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica starts with the Lady Jessica side face up. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications; FAQ & Rulings: Reverend Mother Jessica.

answers.answer: For Margot and Irulan, moving from 1 to 3 counts as reaching 2; the same Faction can count as reached again after losing Influence and later moving up to 2. Moving down through 2 does not count. Moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard during Clean Up does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from your hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Lady Margot Fenring / Princess Irulan and Spacing Guild's Favor.

answers.answer: Accept Contract (Spice Trade) has no cost: draw a card and take a contract with CHOAM, otherwise gain 2 Solari (including when none remain). Dutiful Service (Emperor) has no cost: gain 1 Emperor Influence and take a contract, or 2 Solari without CHOAM/when none remain. Accept Contract does not advance a Faction track automatically; Dutiful Service is an Emperor space and grants 1 Emperor Influence. Each advances only as stated, with no additional double Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Accept Contract and Dutiful Service; only actual Faction board spaces automatically give their Influence.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, recruit one troop and draw one card; Combat. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw one card; Combat. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, recruit two troops and draw two cards; Combat.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table.

answers.answer: Deep Desert (Spice Trade, Combat) costs 3 water, gives all bonus spice, then choose 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, summon two worms. Hagga Basin (Spice Trade, Combat) costs 1 water, gives all bonus spice, then choose 2 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, summon one worm. Bonus spice is gained either way; Hooks are not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Sandworms: Hooks are retained, not spent.

answers.answer: Sietch Tabr (City, Combat) requires 2+ Fremen Influence. Choose either: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water; or gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The Shield Wall option does not grant a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr.

answers.answer: High Council (Landsraad) costs 5 Solari each visit. First visit: place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Later visits: gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops. It is not marked Combat.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council; non-Combat status definition.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone has one and 6 once anyone has one. Each player may visit only once per game. The third Agent becomes available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival gaining its Swordmaster also reduces human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Swordmaster.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege uses the Landsraad icon, requires 2+ Emperor Influence, and costs 3 Solari. Its effects: you may discard an Intrigue to draw one, then recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It can recall any other Agent you own on the board; visiting does not automatically grant Emperor Influence because it is not an Emperor Faction space.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege; board-space guide note that it is not a Faction-icon space.

answers.answer: Shipping uses the Spice Trade icon, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; that Influence need not be with the Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Shipping.

answers.answer: Gather Support (Landsraad, non-Combat) costs either 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops, and if paying 2 Solari also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery (City, Combat) costs either 0 or 1 spice; gain 2 Solari, or 4 Solari if you pay 1 spice. Its controller also gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries: Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner (Spacing Guild, Combat): cost 5 spice; gain 1 Guild Influence and recruit five troops. Desert Tactics (Fremen, Combat): cost 1 water; gain 1 Fremen Influence, recruit one troop, optionally trash a card. Sardaukar (Emperor, not marked Combat): cost 4 spice; gain 1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue, recruit four troops. Normal deployment is allowed at Heighliner and Desert Tactics only.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries; Combat spaces permit normal deployment.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall (Landsraad): no cost; draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn if your Agent is still there. Espionage (Bene Gesserit): costs 1 spice; gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies (Spacing Guild): no cost; gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water. Assembly Hall's Persuasion is used during Reveal, conditional on the Agent remaining there.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide entries: Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn; it may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when the card gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it through other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Manipulate.

answers.answer: The standard two-player Rival gets a color, four cubes at bottom Influence spaces, three troops in garrison and remaining troops in supply, two Agents in supply with Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies, and 1 water; score and Combat marker start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival's 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall and it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup and opening description.

answers.answer: As soon as its combined resources reach its printed Swordmaster threshold, it spends that many, prioritizing Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, then water. It keeps leftovers. Its third Agent can be used in the current round.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, it spends each set of 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP. A mixed total of seven resources does not qualify; the sets must match one of those exact resource types and quantities.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: after Swordmaster, whenever it has 7 Solari, 7 spice, 3 Intrigue, or 3 water, spend such set for 1 VP.

answers.answer: A Rival takes Influence in the Faction with least Influence, breaking ties by the leftmost icon on its priority list. It gains/loses Influence VP and Alliance VP like a human, but does not receive the resource bonus for reaching 4 Influence. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means the position in its Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Resources and Swordmaster; Combat; Agent turns.

answers.answer: No. It selects only the condition-matching destination; if that destination is occupied, it reveals a new card rather than using the other. The two-destination cards are selected by Guild Influence for Accept Contract/Shipping or Conflict tier for Deliver Supplies/Heighliner.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space, a Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the Hagal card recruited none. Troops recruited at a non-Combat space go into its garrison. A conditional 2+ Influence bonus not met does not prevent Agent placement; only that bonus is missed.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns, troop icons and Combat deployment.

answers.answer: For an unrestricted Spy, use the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. A specified post must be empty or placement is ignored. Placing the third/final supply Spy recalls the other two and triggers the Rival's printed Scheme. Rivals never Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If a Scheme recruits troops before the Agent placement and the Rival then visits a Combat space that turn, those recruited troops deploy too. If a Place Spy card has no legal post, ignore the placement and reveal another Hagal card because it has not sent an Agent.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: The Rival always collects accumulated bonus spice at a visited Maker space. At Hagga Basin/Deep Desert, if it has Hooks and the Conflict permits worms, it summons one/two worms instead of taking base spice. Without Hooks or when the Conflict is protected, it summons none and takes base spice (2/4); Imperial Basin always gives 1 base spice. Hooks are gained if a Hagal Hooks icon appears and it lacks them.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Maker spaces.

answers.answer: At the beginning of Combat, if the Rival has at least one deployed unit, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add its bottom swords as strength, ignoring other content. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A unit-free Rival gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Combat.

answers.answer: Yes. Rivals can gain control, receive the defensive troop from supply, score battle-icon VP and double rewards with worms normally. It always takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay resources or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; under CHOAM a contract reward gives it 2 Solari.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Combat.

answers.answer: During Reveal resolution, total strength, announce it, and set the Combat marker at any point; update it as needed during the turn. Over 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: Resolve Reveal Effects; Actions: Strength.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring to send an Agent on an Agent turn. Merely revealing the card does not activate it. Card text of any type can override normal game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup: Leader abilities; Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: The Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. The icon by itself is a return instruction; it is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard-a-card instruction cannot discard an Intrigue unless it specifies Intrigue cards.
answers.evidence: Trashing; Discarding.

answers.answer: When a Conflict reward granting one chosen Influence is doubled by a sandworm, you may take two Influence with the same Faction or with two different Factions. By contrast, a single effect granting two free-choice Influence must put both in one Faction; it cannot be split.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example; Influence: free-choice two cannot be split.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival's own Signet Ring ability as printed on its Rival card; no human Signet Ring card or Rival Reveal turn is needed. The Rival follows its printed Signet Ring and takes Agent turns, never a Reveal turn. The summary does not give the specific text of any particular Rival card's Signet Ring ability.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: follow its printed Signet Ring abilities; Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
